refs.quote: AUGMENTIN is a combination of amoxicillin, a penicillin-class antibacterial and clavulanate potassium, a beta‑lactamase inhibitor indicated for treatment of the following infections in adults and pediatric patients:

tall_man.note: Not listed in FDA/ISMP Tall Man list; generic name lowercase per EXTRACTION.md

regimens.indication: Severe Infections and Infections of the Respiratory Tract (LRTI, Sinusitis, Otitis Media, Skin/Skin Structure, UTI) — Adults and Pediatric Patients >= 40 kg (q12h)

refs.quote: AUGMENTIN is indicated for the treatment of infections in adults and pediatric patients, due to susceptible isolates of the designated bacteria in the conditions listed below: Lower Respiratory Tract Infections - caused by beta‑lactamase–producing isolates of Haemophilus influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis .
Severe infections and infections of the respiratory tract one 875 mg tablet a of AUGMENTIN every 12 hours or one 500 mg tablet b,c of AUGMENTIN every 8 hours

regimens.dose_text: One 875 mg/125 mg tablet every 12 hours (based on amoxicillin component). Take at the start of a meal to minimize GI intolerance and enhance clavulanate absorption.

regimens.indication: Severe Infections and Infections of the Respiratory Tract — Adults and Pediatric Patients >= 40 kg (q8h)

refs.quote: Severe infections and infections of the respiratory tract one 875 mg tablet a of AUGMENTIN every 12 hours or one 500 mg tablet b,c of AUGMENTIN every 8 hours

regimens.dose_text: One 500 mg/125 mg tablet every 8 hours (based on amoxicillin component). Two 250 mg/125 mg tablets are NOT substitutable for one 500 mg/125 mg tablet.

regimens.indication: Less Severe Infections (Skin/Skin Structure, UTI, Mild Respiratory) — Adults and Pediatric Patients >= 40 kg (q12h)

refs.quote: Less severe infections one 500 mg tablet b,c of AUGMENTIN every 12 hours or one 250 mg tablet d of AUGMENTIN every 8 hours

regimens.dose_text: One 500 mg/125 mg tablet every 12 hours (based on amoxicillin component).

regimens.indication: Less Severe Infections — Adults and Pediatric Patients >= 40 kg (q8h)

refs.quote: Less severe infections one 500 mg tablet b,c of AUGMENTIN every 12 hours or one 250 mg tablet d of AUGMENTIN every 8 hours

regimens.dose_text: One 250 mg/125 mg tablet every 8 hours (based on amoxicillin component). Do NOT use 250 mg/125 mg tablet until child weighs >= 40 kg; not substitutable with 250 mg/62.5 mg chewable tablet.

regimens.indication: Pediatric Patients Aged 12 Weeks (3 Months) and Older (< 40 kg) — q12h Regimen

refs.quote: Pediatric patients aged 12 weeks (3 months) and older: 25 to 45 mg/kg/day every 12 hours or 20 to 40 mg/kg/day every 8 hours, up to the adult dose.
The every 12 hour regimen is recommended as it is associated with significantly less diarrhea

regimens.dose_text: 25 to 45 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours (based on the amoxicillin component), up to the adult dose. The every 12 hour regimen is recommended as it is associated with significantly less diarrhea.

regimens.indication: Pediatric Patients Aged 12 Weeks (3 Months) and Older (< 40 kg) — q8h Regimen

refs.quote: Pediatric patients aged 12 weeks (3 months) and older: 25 to 45 mg/kg/day every 12 hours or 20 to 40 mg/kg/day every 8 hours, up to the adult dose.

regimens.dose_text: 20 to 40 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours (based on the amoxicillin component), up to the adult dose.

regimens.indication: Neonates and Infants Aged Less Than 12 Weeks (Less Than 3 Months)

refs.quote: Neonates and Infants aged less than 12 weeks (less than 3 months) 30 mg/kg/day every 12 hours a Experience with the AUGMENTIN 200 mg/28.5 mg per 5 mL formulation in this age group is limited, and thus, use of the AUGMENTIN 125 mg/31.25 mg per 5 mL for oral suspension is recommended.

regimens.dose_text: 30 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours (based on the amoxicillin component). Use of the 125 mg/31.25 mg per 5 mL oral suspension is recommended.

refs.quote: Renal impairment patients with a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of less than 30 mL/min should NOT receive the 875 mg dose (based on the amoxicillin component) of AUGMENTIN.

renal_impairment.description: Patients with impaired renal function do not generally require dose reduction unless impairment is severe (GFR < 30 mL/min). Patients with GFR < 30 mL/min should NOT receive the 875 mg dose.

hepatic.value: Contraindicated in patients with a previous history of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction associated with amoxicillin/clavulanate. Hepatic dysfunction (usually reversible, though deaths reported) occurs more commonly in the elderly, males, or on prolonged treatment; no specific dose adjustment provided.

refs.quote: AUGMENTIN is contraindicated in patients with a previous history of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction associated with AUGMENTIN.

Hepatic dysfunction, including hepatitis and cholestatic jaundice, increases in serum transaminases (AST and/or ALT), serum bilirubin, and/or alkaline phosphatase, has been reported with Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium. It has been reported more commonly in the elderly, in males, or in patients on prolonged treatment.
AUGMENTIN is an oral antibacterial combination consisting of amoxicillin and the beta‑lactamase inhibitor, clavulanate potassium (the potassium salt of clavulanic acid).

mg_safety.note: Beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor combination; no myasthenia gravis exacerbation warning in FDA label.

value.instructions: Oral suspension formulations (125 mg/31.25 mg per 5 mL, 200 mg/28.5 mg per 5 mL, 250 mg/62.5 mg per 5 mL, or 400 mg/57 mg per 5 mL) are available for adults who have difficulty swallowing tablets.

refs.quote: Adults who have difficulty swallowing may be given the AUGMENTIN 200 mg/28.5 mg per 5 mL suspension or the AUGMENTIN 400 mg/57 mg per 5 mL suspension may be used in place of the 875 mg/125 mg tablet.
Skin and Appendages: Rashes, pruritus, urticaria, erythema multiforme, SJS, TEN, DRESS, AGEP, exfoliative dermatitis , and linear IgA dermatosis.
Central Nervous System: Agitation, anxiety, behavioral changes, aseptic meningitis, confusion, convulsions, dizziness, insomnia, and reversible hyperactivity have been reported.
The most frequently reported adverse effects were diarrhea/loose stools (9%), nausea (3%), skin rashes and urticaria (3%), vomiting (1%) and vaginitis (1%).

value: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SJS, TEN, DRESS, AGEP, exfoliative dermatitis)
Hepatic dysfunction (hepatitis, cholestatic jaundice; deaths reported)

refs.quote: Immune: Hypersensitivity reactions, anaphylactic/anaphylactoid reactions (including shock), angioedema, serum sickness-like reactions (urticaria or skin rash accompanied by arthritis, arthralgia, myalgia, and frequently fever), hypersensitivity vasculitis

The onset of signs/symptoms of hepatic dysfunction may occur during or several weeks after therapy has been discontinued. The hepatic dysfunction, which may be severe, is usually reversible. Deaths have been reported

mechanism_of_action.value: Amoxicillin is a semisynthetic penicillin-class antibacterial with bactericidal activity against susceptible Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria; clavulanic acid is a beta-lactam that inactivates beta-lactamase enzymes, protecting amoxicillin from degradation.

refs.quote: The formulation of amoxicillin and clavulanic acid in AUGMENTIN protects amoxicillin from degradation by some beta-lactamase enzymes and extends the antibacterial spectrum of amoxicillin to include many bacteria normally resistant to amoxicillin.

value.metabolism: Approximately 50% to 70% of amoxicillin and 25% to 40% of clavulanic acid are excreted unchanged in urine during the first 6 hours.

refs.quote: Approximately 50% to 70% of the amoxicillin and approximately 25% to 40% of the clavulanic acid are excreted unchanged in urine during the first 6 hours after administration of a single 250 mg/125 mg or 500 mg/125 mg tablet of AUGMENTIN.

value.effect: Probenecid decreases renal tubular secretion of amoxicillin (not clavulanic acid), resulting in increased and prolonged blood concentrations of amoxicillin.
value.management: Co-administration of probenecid is not recommended.

refs.quote: Probenecid decreases the renal tubular secretion of amoxicillin but does not delay renal excretion of clavulanic acid. Concurrent use with AUGMENTIN may result in increased and prolonged blood concentrations of amoxicillin. Co-administration of probenecid is not recommended.

value.effect: Abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time (increased INR) has been reported in patients receiving amoxicillin and oral anticoagulants.
value.management: Undertake appropriate monitoring when anticoagulants are prescribed concurrently; adjustments in oral anticoagulant dose may be necessary.

refs.quote: Abnormal prolongation of prothrombin time (increased international normalized ratio [INR]) has been reported in patients receiving amoxicillin and oral anticoagulants. Appropriate monitoring should be undertaken when anticoagulants are prescribed concurrently with AUGMENTIN. Adjustments in the dose of oral anticoagulants may be necessary to maintain the desired level of anticoagulation.

value.effect: Concurrent administration of allopurinol and amoxicillin increases the incidence of rashes compared to amoxicillin alone.
value.management: Monitor for cutaneous rash when co-administered.

refs.quote: The concurrent administration of allopurinol and amoxicillin increases the incidence of rashes in patients receiving both drugs as compared to patients receiving amoxicillin alone.

value.effect: May affect intestinal flora, leading to lower estrogen reabsorption and reduced efficacy of combined oral contraceptives.
value.management: Advise patients of potential reduced contraceptive efficacy and consider backup contraception.

refs.quote: AUGMENTIN may affect intestinal flora, leading to lower estrogen reabsorption and reduced efficacy of combined oral estrogen/progesterone contraceptives.

Co‑administration with probenecid is not recommended. ( 7.1 ) Concomitant use of AUGMENTIN and oral anticoagulants may increase the prolongation of prothrombin time.( 7.2 ) Co-administration with allopurinol increases the risk of rash. ( 7.3 ) AUGMENTIN may reduce efficacy of oral contraceptives. ( 7.4 )

tier.note: Pregnancy Category B: animal reproduction studies up to 1200 mg/kg/day (2-4x human amoxicillin BSA dose) showed no fetal harm, but there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; label states 'should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed.'

refs.quote: Pregnancy Category B. Reproduction studies performed in pregnant rats and mice given AUGMENTIN (2:1 ratio formulation of amoxicillin:clavulanate) at oral doses up to 1200 mg/kg/day revealed no evidence of harm to the fetus due to AUGMENTIN.

There are, however, no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Because animal reproduction studies are not always predictive of human response, this drug should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed.

contraception.value: May reduce efficacy of combined oral estrogen/progesterone contraceptives due to effects on intestinal flora and lower estrogen reabsorption.

refs.quote: AUGMENTIN may affect intestinal flora, leading to lower estrogen reabsorption and reduced efficacy of combined oral estrogen/progesterone contraceptives.

lactation_summary.value: Amoxicillin is excreted in human milk; use by nursing mothers may lead to sensitization of infants; exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman.

refs.quote: Amoxicillin has been shown to be excreted in human milk. Amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium use by nursing mothers may lead to sensitization of infants. Caution should be exercised when amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium is administered to a nursing woman.
